overall: The Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by inaccurately stating in its September 10 minutes that a member's recommendation vote was subject to review of a draft letter; the minutes were otherwise accurate and sufficiently detailed, and the Board was ordered to amend them.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 10 minutes omitted the Chair's and two members' statements that the PRD Plan was preferable to a subdivision, making them insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board’s September 10 meeting minutes substantially comply with the requirement that they provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion at issue.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 10 minutes omitted that a vote was taken to recommend the PRD Plan to the Zoning Board of Appeals.
allegations.key_passage: we find the statement that Mr. Flint’s vote to recommend the PRD Plan would be “subject to review of a draft recommendation letter . . .” to be inaccurate.

remedy: Within 60 days of receipt of the letter, the Board must amend its September 10 meeting minutes to accurately reflect the discussion.
remedy_passage: We order that within sixty (60) days of receipt of this letter the Board amend its September 10 meeting minutes as discussed above.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
